sources.entry: 30 Days of JavaScript: 30 days of JavaScript programming challenge is a step-by-step guide to learn JavaScript programming language in 30 days.

summary.one_liner: A 30-day, step-by-step JavaScript tutorial course that teaches the language from basics to mini projects, one topic per day.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a daily tutorial series covering JavaScript from setup through 30 topics, listed in a table of contents: data types, variables, conditionals, arrays, loops, functions, objects, higher-order functions, sets and maps, destructuring, regular expressions, error handling, classes, JSON, web storage, promises, closures, clean code, and DOM manipulation. The README shown covers only Day 1 in full, which includes installing Node.js, using the Chrome console, writing inline, internal, and external scripts, and explaining primitive types, typeof, comments, and let/const/var. Each day ends with numbered exercises. Days 24 to 29 are mini projects (solar system, world countries data visualization, portfolio, leaderboard, animated characters) and Day 30 is final projects. The README points to translations in several languages and a video companion on YouTube.
use_cases: build small DOM and mini projects
how_to_run: Install Node.js (optional, recommended v14 at time of writing)
Open Google Chrome developer console and run console.log examples
Create a project folder with an index.html file
Add JavaScript inline, internal, or as an external .js file linked from the HTML
Open index.html in a browser and check the console output
Work through each day's topics and exercises in order
notable: Organized as 30 daily lessons with a topic table and numbered exercises each day
Written in conversational English aimed at beginners and advanced developers alike
Covers browser-based JavaScript first, then DOM and mini projects
Available in many languages (English, Spanish, Italian, Russian, Turkish, Korean, Vietnamese, Polish, Portuguese, and more)
caveats: A completion certificate requires enrolling in DevOsome, an external platform
The README excerpt covers only Day 1 in full; later days are listed but not shown
Recommends against using var, and the Node.js version information is dated
